solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Glaring malevolently, putting support round farm animal

indicators.note: to put something round another is to wrap it about, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a sling is a strap that supports an injured arm
a cow is a farm animal

explanation.surface: Someone glares angrily while propping up a farm animal with a support.
explanation.walkthrough: The support is wrapped around the animal: S-COW-LING.
explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is to frown with an angry look, so scowling describes a fierce, hostile stare.

clue.text: Nameless bird, ultimately with scant illumination

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so without a name means one letter is dropped
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of each following word is kept

blocks.note: a starling is a bird; it loses its N
the last letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A bird without a name flies by in dim light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scant illumination' looks like the definition, but 'scant' gives a letter; the definition is just 'illumination'.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlight is the faint light given off by the stars at night, a form of natural lighting.

clue.text: Marmalade cat in Florida city?

blocks.note: first meaning: the ginger cat of Kathleen Hale's classic children's picture books
second meaning: the city in central Florida, home of Disney World

explanation.walkthrough: Orlando the Marmalade Cat is the hero of a series of British children's books; 'marmalade' describes his orange coat. The same name belongs to a city in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: The storybook ginger tom and the large Florida tourist city share the same proper name.

clue.text: Singer allowed to entertain pub

indicators.note: a host who entertains has a guest inside the house, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: let means allowed
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A singer is permitted to perform at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a human performer, but here it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small finch prized for its song, so crosswords call it a singer.

clue.text: Sustained robin finally, one trapped in your and my outhouse

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the word is used
something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: the last letter of robin
what belongs to you and me is ours
I is the Roman numeral one
a shed is an outhouse

explanation.surface: A robin is fed through the winter after getting stuck in a shared garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your and my' is an unusual way of saying 'our', which is easy to miss; the trapped one sits between the two words it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To nourish is to feed and keep alive, so a well-fed creature has been sustained.

clue.text: Initially some plays only occasionally featured such burlesques

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.clueFragment: some plays only occasionally featured such
blocks.note: the first letters of these six words

explanation.surface: Only now and then do some theatre programmes include such comic send-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' looks like a signal to take alternate letters, but it is just part of the fodder; 'Initially' covers every word.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a mocking imitation of a serious work, which is exactly what a spoof is.

clue.text: Extremely sensitive singer consuming a fish

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the two outer letters of the word are kept
to consume is to take inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the first and last letters of sensitive
taken as written
a bass is a singer with the lowest voice

explanation.surface: A very touchy vocalist is eating a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters and the singer together swallow A between them: SE-A-BASS.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bass is a common European food fish, a perch-like species of coastal waters.

clue.text: A coy girl unhappily accepting Heath’s first minority government

indicators.note: something unhappily placed is upset, so these letters are thrown into a new order
first points to the opening, so only the initial letter of the name is used
to accept is to take in, so one piece is received inside another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the first letter of Heath

explanation.surface: A shy young woman is unhappy to receive Edward Heath's first minority government.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British Conservative prime minister, which makes the political surface plausible; his initial goes into the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is rule by a small privileged group, literally government by the few.

clue.text: Obscure king crossing bar, a hazard at sea

blocks.note: to fog is to obscure
to bar is to ban
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An unknown monarch crosses a sandbar, which is risky at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The king comes last, after the bar; 'crossing' only places him beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense bank of mist over water hides rocks and ships, making it a real danger to sailors.

clue.text: Worry principally about endless evil

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first of all, so the opening letter is taken
with no end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the first letter of about
ill means evil; it loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone frets chiefly about never-ending wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL as in 'ill will' means evil; trimmed it gives IL.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail can mean to trouble or afflict, as in 'what ails you?', a sense close to worry.

clue.text: Repulsive new audience accommodation a university installed

indicators.note: something installed is fitted into place, so one piece is set inside another

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
seating is where an audience sits
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A new theatre's seating, put in by a university, is horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: A and U go in between N and SEATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nauseating makes you feel sick with disgust, so it is repulsive.

clue.text: Hang about, initially investigating expensive underwear

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each following word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: to linger is to hang about
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone tells a shopper to wait before looking into pricey underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang about' sounds like a spoken 'wait a minute', but it is the verb to loiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underclothing, usually the fine or decorative kind.

clue.text: Crazy, sacrificing last of rhubarb for pineapple!

indicators.note: to sacrifice something is to give it up, so a letter is dropped
last of points to the final letter of the next word as the letter given up

blocks.note: bananas is slang for crazy
the last letter of rhubarb, which is the letter removed

explanation.surface: It's mad to give up rhubarb for a pineapple!
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letter is B, the end of rhubarb, taken from the front of the slang word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the botanical genus and the name in many languages for the pineapple fruit.

clue.text: One of two giants crushing head of reckless spirit?

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the first letter of the word is used
something crushed is squeezed in a grip, so one piece is pressed inside another

blocks.note: Gog and Magog are the two legendary giants of London
the first letter of reckless

explanation.surface: A giant stamps on a reckless person's head; the question mark admits the spirit is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are giants of British legend whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall. The question mark flags that grog is diluted spirit rather than spirit itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Grog was rum mixed with water served to sailors, and the word loosely means any alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Gloomy detectives in burial ground

blocks.note: grave means solemn and gloomy
the Yard is Scotland Yard, the London police detectives

explanation.surface: Sombre detectives investigate in a cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but it only joins wordplay to definition. Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is a plot of land, often by a church, where the dead are buried.

clue.text: Revolutionary directions: encrust rich tart

blocks.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
east, south, east: compass points
to cake is to coat thickly, to encrust

explanation.surface: A revolutionary issues orders to put a crust on a rich tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a reversal signal, but it is Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesecake is a rich dessert of sweetened soft cheese on a biscuit base, a kind of open tart.

clue.text: Eurasian rose, say, worker planted in row

indicators.note: something planted in is set into the ground, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, or say
a row is a line
a worker ant; worker is a common crossword word for ant

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a Eurasian rose in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker goes inside the row, with EG in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose of Europe and Asia with fragrant leaves.

clue.text: Fill in rowing crew about northern lake in French

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round others

blocks.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
N is the abbreviation for northern
L is the abbreviation for lake
en is the French for in

explanation.surface: A rowing crew trains around a northern lake in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fill in' looks like part of the wordplay, but it is the definition: to tell someone the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill someone in is to inform them, and to enlighten is to give knowledge or explanation.

clue.text: Swindle at seat of Irish kings? A harmless lie

blocks.note: the Hill of Tara was the seat of the High Kings of Ireland
to diddle is to swindle

explanation.surface: A con at the ancient royal seat of Ireland turns out to be a fib.
explanation.walkthrough: The swindle sits 'at' the seat, so it comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A taradiddle is a petty falsehood or fib, a lie told without serious intent to harm.

clue.text: Object in lorry leaving Edinburgh for starters

indicators.note: starters are the first course, so the opening letters of each word are used

blocks.note: an artic is an articulated lorry
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Something in a truck is left behind as it departs Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a particular thing or item, which is what an object is.

clue.text: Trendy regular sweetheart, not unknown as an alternative

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend
Y is a mathematical unknown, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A fashionable person's steady partner is not a mystery, so someone else is chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, so 'unknown' supplies a letter to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, that is, as a substitute or other choice.

clue.text: Means to reverse large sailing vessel

indicators.note: reversing goes backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a way is a means
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A way to back up a big sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like a link word, but it is the word to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing boat with a small mizzen mast behind the rudder post.

clue.text: Car British Leyland originally made, ultimately capable of being caught

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so the opening letters are taken
ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is taken

blocks.note: Audi is a German car make
the first letters of these two words
the last letter of made

explanation.surface: A car the old British Leyland company built that you could hear coming.
explanation.walkthrough: British Leyland was the nationalised British carmaker of the 1970s, known as BL.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a remark is to hear it, so something audible can be caught by the ear.

clue.text: Change sides? That’s a fault

blocks.note: first meaning, a verb: to desert one's country or party for the other side
second meaning, a noun: a flaw or imperfection

explanation.walkthrough: The question then answer looks like a moral judgment on turncoats; it is two senses of one word, stressed differently.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to abandon allegiance; as a noun it means a shortcoming or flaw.

clue.text: Tension revealed by female teacher avoiding motorway

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: a schoolmistress, or mistress, is a female teacher
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, read as MI

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher shows how tense she is by keeping off the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords read its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or physical strain, which is a close synonym for tension.

clue.text: Insufficiently cook goulash at first, being of little influence

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; read 'being' as a noun: a being of little influence

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: to underdo food is to cook it too little
the first letter of goulash

explanation.surface: Undercooking the goulash at the start means it lacks punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a creature, here one with little clout.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the weaker party expected to lose, someone with little power or standing.

clue.text: Talk with woman, the mistress of the house

blocks.note: to chat is to talk
Elaine is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone talks with a woman who runs the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine was the lady in charge of a castle or large household, keeping its keys.

clue.text: Bishop attending cricket club

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to be at a place is to attend it

explanation.surface: A bishop goes along to the local cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket club' looks like a society; it is the club a batsman holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bat is the wooden implement used to hit the ball, which the clue calls a club.

clue.text: Required to be worked like dough, we’re told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than seen, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: dough worked by hand is kneaded

explanation.surface: Bread dough has to be worked, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the baking word is silent, so both words are said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed means wanted or necessary, which is what required means.

clue.text: Find out about article made of tanned hide once

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to learn is to find out
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Discover something about an old item made from tanned skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the word as old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathern is an archaic adjective meaning made of leather, which is tanned animal hide.
